title: Scaled credit allowance: hiring & SLA impact matrix
body:
Purpose:
A compact scenario workbook to evaluate how offering scaled pre-paid credit allowances (volume-tiered credits sold to customers) changes our hiring cadence, SLA staffing coverage, and near-term revenue recognition risk. This is intended as a quick-finance + GTM decision support sheet during Q3 planning.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- If we increase credit allowances (aggressive upfront discounts for larger pre-purchases) we see near-term ARR acceleration but materially higher token throughput volatility, which pushes hiring earlier for SRE/infra and increases Dedicated GPU commitments.
- Three tested commitment tiers (Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive) show a tradeoff between upfront cash inflow and probability of SLA breaches in month-on-month peak weeks.
- Recommended: adopt Balanced tier with a set of trigger rules for staggered hiring (2 phased SRE hires + 1 infra commit) and a 60-day runway buffer before auto-bursting Dedicated capacity.

Key assumptions (base-case unless noted):
- Average price per 1k tokens (hosted) baseline: $0.80.
- Pre-paid credit discount bands: 10% (Small), 20% (Medium), 35% (Large).
- Customer behavior elasticity: Medium-tier customers increase token usage +40% in month 0 after purchase; Large-tier customers +120% in month 0, then normalizes to +20% thereafter.
- Baseline capacity mix: 55% spot GPU, 30% reserved Dedicated, 15% burst capacity (cloud).
- SLA target: 99.5% monthly availability; threshold for action: any scenario where weekly latency SLO misses >2% probability in simulated month.

Scenario matrix (summary results):
| Scenario   | Upfront cash delta vs baseline | Peak weekly token delta | Estimated incremental hires (6mo) | SLA miss risk (month 1) | Recommended immediate action |
| Conservative | +$1.2M | +18% | +2 (1 SRE, 1 infra) | 1.1% | Monitor / pre-stage 1 infra node |
| Balanced     | +$4.8M | +45% | +4 (2 SRE, 1 infra, 1 capacity eng) | 2.9% | Phase hires + trigger at 30% sustained growth |
| Aggressive   | +$11.5M | +120% | +8 (3 SRE, 3 infra ops, 2 capacity planners) | 9.6% | Immediate hiring + Dedicated commit + capacity hedge |
Note: numbers are rounded and represent median of 1,000 Monte Carlo simulated customer adoption patterns with stochastic weekly spikes.

Headcount phasing (proposed ramp for Balanced scenario):
- Month 0 (post-launch): hire 1 Senior SRE (onboard week 3) and 1 Capacity Engineer (contract 3 months)
- Month 1: onboard 1 infra ops (mid-senior) and initiate Dedicated GPU 3-month reserve contract (small bucket)
- Month 2-4: hire 1 Reliability Eng (mid) and convert contract capacity to reserved if usage persists >35% above baseline for 6 weeks
- Contingency months (if spikes >70%): accelerate 2 contractor SREs and unlock cloud burst pool (pre-negotiated pricing)

Cost impacts (6-month window, Balanced):
- Incremental opex (salaries + onboarding + contractor): ~$720k
- Incremental infra commit (reserved GPU partial bucket): ~$560k
- Net cash after discounts + immediate recognition (assume 60% recognized in month 0 per revenue policy): +$2.9M net present inflow in month 0
- Payback horizon: 8-10 months under baseline churn; 6-8 months if usage retention > baseline by +20%

Sensitivity slices (what changes decision):
- If Large-tier customer elasticity is only +60% instead of +120%, Aggressive becomes materially less attractive (SLA miss risk drops ~4ppt).
- If churn increases by +5ppt due to discounted pricing, effective ARR drops 12% over 12 months and headcount payback extends >14 months.
- If median weekly spike variance doubles (higher burstiness), Dedicated commit requirement and SRE hires both increase ~30% relative to median run.

Micro-sim output (representative rows from simulation):
- Median week peak multiplier (Balanced): 1.45; 95th percentile: 2.1
- Median additional GPU-hours/week (Balanced): +14k GPU-hours; 95th pct: +36k
- Median token-runrate delta: +45% centered, stdev 22%

Trigger rules (operationalized):
1) Trigger A (Soft): sustained >25% token usage growth over 3 consecutive weeks -> onboard next queued infra engineer (estimate 6-week lead).
2) Trigger B (Medium): any single-week spike >50% over baseline -> enable contracted capacity pool (cost +10% margin) and start expedited SRE recruitment.
3) Trigger C (Hard): sustained >60% growth + 95th percentile latency degradation -> execute reserved Dedicated commit (minimum 3-month) and hire 2 senior SREs or convert contractors.

Recommended pricing guardrails (to protect unit economics):
- Cap Deep discount (>=35%) offers to customers with predicted LTV > 18x acquisition cost and minimum 6-month non-cancelable term.
- Attach a usage smoothing clause: customers get 70% of discount if usage remains within expected envelope; additional top-up credit if usage materially exceeds prediction (reduces surprise).

Open questions / data needs (prioritize):
- Per-account elasticity by cohort: need top-50 customers elasticity estimate (data science).
- 12-month churn impact of heavy discounts (historical A/B or cohort analog).
- Cost to rapidly convert cloud burst to reserved in major regions (sales + infra procurement).

Next steps (owners and timeline):
- Finance to finalize cash recognition run for proposed Balanced tier and produce P&L waterfall (Priya) - due 2025-09-08.
- Solutions/GTM to draft customer eligibility criteria and sample commercial term (Marco + Ellen) - due 2025-09-05.
- Eng infra to validate lead times for infra hires and Dedicated commit negotiation (Owen) - due 2025-09-10.

Appendix (quick model snapshots):
- Spreadsheets used: pricing-sim/balanced-vs-aggr.xlsx (internal)
- Key assumptions encoded: discount_band, elasticity_by_size, churn_delta_by_discount, cost_per_gpu_hour, reserved_lead_time_weeks

Notes to reviewers: this sheet is intentionally compact — it omits detailed cohort churn tables to keep decision conversation focused. If we move forward with Balanced, we'll publish a separate, fully annotated workbook with per-customer modeled outputs and week-level provisioning forecasts.

Unresolved: whether legal can add a short minimum-usage clause into standard T&Cs without undue sales friction (tag: Legal review).

End of sheet.
